common.journeyOutroText: Twelve places, one route — there's plenty more to discover beyond this itinerary.

pendjari.name: Pendjari National Park
pendjari.tagline: Large protected area in the northwest
pendjari.description: Large protected area in the northwest of the country, Atacora savannas and cliffs, emblematic wildlife (lions, elephants, hippopotamuses).

tanongou.name: Tanongou Falls
tanongou.tagline: Waterfall and natural pool in the Atacora chain
tanongou.description: Waterfall and natural pool in the Atacora chain.

dassa.name: Dassa-Zoumè Hills
dassa.description: Around forty granite hills, caves and sanctuaries, a place of Marian pilgrimage and Vodun traditions.

abomey.name: Royal Palaces of Abomey
abomey.tagline: Former capital of the Danxomè kingdom
abomey.description: Former capital of the Danxomè (Dahomey) kingdom, palaces of the twelve kings adorned with bas-reliefs, classified as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

ouidah.name: Ouidah
ouidah.tagline: Former trading post on the transatlantic slave trade route
ouidah.description: Former trading post on the transatlantic slave trade route (Slave Route, Door of No Return), also the cradle of the Vodun cult (Temple of Pythons, international Vodun festival).

foret-kpasse.name: Kpassè Sacred Forest
foret-kpasse.tagline: Forest island in the heart of Ouidah
foret-kpasse.description: Forest island in the heart of Ouidah (about 4 hectares today, compared to about thirty originally), dedicated to King Kpassè, legendary founder of the city, whose spirit is said to be incarnated in a sacred tree (iroko) at its center. Also operates as an open-air museum: statues of Vodun deities (Mami Wata, Gou, Tolègba...), notably those of sculptor Cyprien Tokoudagba. Site of ritual ceremonies.

ganvie.name: Ganvié
ganvie.description: Lake village built on stilts in the middle of Lake Nokoué.

cotonou.name: Cotonou
cotonou.description: Largest city and economic lung of the country, Dantokpa market, booming art scene.

amazone.name: Amazon Monument
amazone.description: Monumental bronze statue 30 meters high (about 150 tons), inaugurated on July 30, 2022, on the Amazones esplanade in Cotonou, facing the Atlantic Ocean. Work of the Chinese sculptor Li Xiangqun, it pays tribute to the Agoodjié — the Amazons of Dahomey, an all-female military regiment active until the end of the 19th century. It is the second largest statue in Africa after the African Renaissance Monument in Dakar.
amazone.fact: 30 meters, tribute to the Agoodjié warriors

bio-guera.name: Bio Guéra Monument
bio-guera.description: Equestrian statue of bronze, copper and steel (about 7 meters high, 13 tons), erected at the roundabout of the Cotonou international airport and inaugurated on July 30, 2022. It honors Bio Guéra, prince of the Bariba kingdom and Wasangari warlord, a figure of resistance to the French colonial conquest at the end of the 19th century, who died in 1916 near Bembéréké.

porto-novo.name: Porto-Novo
porto-novo.description: Official capital of Benin, Afro-Brazilian architecture, royal palace, Yoruba influences.

grand-popo.name: Grand-Popo
grand-popo.tagline: Quiet beaches at the mouth of the Mono river
grand-popo.description: Quiet beaches at the mouth of the Mono river.
